curriculum_metadata.subject: General Paper
curriculum_metadata.source_document: ADVANCED LEVEL SECONDARY CURRICULUM GENERAL PAPER SYLLABUS.pdf

values: Respect for humanity and the environment
Honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times
Integrity, moral uprightness, and sound character

themes.theme_description: Independent investigation and solution proposal for societal problems.

topics.core_competency: The learner devises innovative ways of solving societal problems through carrying out an independent investigation and proposing feasible solutions in order to improve community wellbeing.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: carry out individual research projects on a societal challenge and present findings in an Extended Essay between 3,000-4,000 words. (k, u, s, v/a)

must_cover: Social Issues: Understanding society, Types of social groups, Individuals: their social roles and responsibilities, Challenges and impact of social groups, Ways of addressing social group challenges, Peer pressure and growing up, Health: medicine, personal hygiene, mental health, drugs and addictions, managing stress and relationships

Culture: Exploring culture, Aspects of culture (music, dance and drama, sports, games and leisure), Appreciate culture and its impact on character formation (customs, traditions, values), Language and culture, Cultural artefacts (art and craft, architecture), Development of cultural creativity and tourism (beauty contests, sculpture, national heritage)

Education: Meaning of education, Types of education and their relevance, Purpose of education, Relevance of education to national development, Challenges in education reforms and interventions, Assessment in education

Human Rights: The meaning of human rights, Fundamental human rights, Violation of human rights and repercussions, Activists and organisations that advocate enjoyment and observance of human rights in Uganda

Challenges of Developing Countries: Resources in developing countries (land, human resource, technology and its appropriateness), Obstacles of growth in developing countries (illiteracy, hunger, insecurity and conflicts)
Economics: Economic policies (taxation, inflation), Economic development (investment, economic dependence), Wealth creation and distribution (poverty, unemployment, brain drain)
Globalisation: Aspects of globalisation (cultural, economic, political, social), Causes and effects of globalisation
Agriculture: Agricultural practices: traditional versus modern practices, Types of farming: modern farming techniques, challenges and their solutions

Science and Technology: Physical and natural science, Architecture, Bio-system engineering, Benefits and application of science, Food and nutrition, Challenges involved in science and technology, Relevance of mathematics in society

Historical Perspective: National and international historical events: scramble and partition of Africa, indirect rule, coups, liberation wars, independence struggles, Impact of historical events on society

Politics and Governance: Types and components of political systems: Multipartyism, Federalism, Feudalism, Communism, Autocracy, Democratic Governance, Militarism, Single-party governance, decentralisation, Strengths and weaknesses of the political systems, Organs of governance: the legislature, the judiciary, the executive, Political activism and conflict resolution

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners, individually, do preparatory reading about the topics.
Learners, in groups, discuss the available topics to guide their research activities.
Learners, in groups, formulate research questions under different fields.
Learners, individually, collect and analyse data where applicable.
Learners, individually, write the Extended Essay and a reflective journal.
Learners, individually, present their Extended Essays in a plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: This is a learner-led project, with support from the teacher. Guide the learners to properly document what they have gone through during the process of their individual project.
Provide opportunities for learners to share progress being made on their project for additional guidance and support.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim:
Guidelines for the Individual Project (Extended Essay) An Extended Essay is a form of guided mini research project through which students conduct a simple study on a topic of interest and share their findings with others in writing. It should include the following sections:
1. Title Page/Cover Page: The title page is the first page of the Extended Essay. Every essay must have a title page, which should clearly show the: i) subject. ii) topic of the study. iii) Name, school and the registration number of the candidate. iv) year of study.
2. The topic: This is decided on after critically thinking about a selected society to identify the problems that are affecting the people. The learner identifies a problem to work with and at the end writes an Extended Essay.
3. The contents page/table of contents: This is the roadmap for the learner’s extended essay. It includes the topics, sub-topics and the pages where the named information is found.
4. The introduction and /or background: The introduction is the opening segment of the Extended Essay, serving as a guide for the readers into the subject that the learner is exploring. It should give a hint about the topic that the learner is working on. This is written as a result of critical thinking about society to identify what problems exist.
5. Research guiding questions (or hypothesis): These questions are formulated to help the learner to internalise the topic and they are to guide in garnering the right information and data for the essay.
6. Body of the Essay: This is the main part of the extended essay. It should include some: i) literature that informed/enlightened the learner about the topic. ii) methods used to collect the data for the essay. iii) how the data was analysed.
7. Conclusion: This gives some of the conclusions the learner draws from the internalisation of the problem.
8. Reflection: This will be the conclusion from the reflection journal that the learner has had, from the time that he/she started the research. It will include some of the challenges and changes that she/he encountered.
9. Recommendations: These are given as suggestions emanating from the study that could help to alleviate the problem.
10. References & bibliography: These are references and bibliography sources. They should be well-written according to the selected referencing system and version.
project_requirements.deliverables_verbatim: Extended Essay between 3,000-4,000 words. Reflective journal.

assessment_weightings.notes_verbatim: There will be only one school-based summative assessment at the end of the year. There will no longer be examinations or tests set at the beginning and end of every term. Instead, there will be a summing up of ongoing teacher assessments made in the context of learning, through Activities of Integration assessment. The learners will also be subjected to End of Cycle Assessment for certification.

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim:
The areas (core topics) from which to do an individual project:
1. Social Issues
2. Culture
3. Education
4. Human Rights
5. Challenges of Developing Countries
6. Economics
7. Globalisation
8. Agriculture
9. Science and Technology
10. Historical Perspective
11. Politics and Governance

Each topic has a competency, which is a broad statement that brings out what the learner is expected to do at the end of the topic. The competency is broken down into learning outcomes, for which suggested learning activities and sample assessment strategies are developed as represented in the three columns below... The learning outcome is coded with some letters such as; k, u, s, gs, and v/a for emphasis to the teacher on what to consider during the lesson.
